newsitem.title: INDIA: India CRISIL gives L&T NCD AAA rating.
newsitem.headline: India CRISIL gives L&T NCD AAA rating.

text.p: India's Credit Rating Information Services of India Ltd (CRISIL) said on Friday that Larsen & Toubro Limited's (L&T) a 1.5 billion rupees NCD programme has been assigned a 'AAA' rating.

The company's commercial paper (CP) programme has been enhanced from 1.25 billion to 3 billion rupees and the rating on the programme has been retained at P1+ indicating that the degree of safety regarding payment on the instrument is very strong.
L&T, a multi-business, multi-location company, is an established contracting and engineering company in India with strong technical expertise.

The company is presently structured into eleven business units, which are broadly classified into five groups. The Engineering & Construction group continues to be the largest, accounting for about 53 percent of L&T's turnover in 1996/97, Cement (17.5 percent), Electrical & Electronics Segment (10.5 percent) and Earth Moving Equipment (5.7 percent) were the other large contributors to turnover.
These diversified revenue streams ensure that regardless of cyclical variations in individual businesses aggregate revenues are elatively stable.
L&T's engineering, procurement and construction division offers industrial fabrication and Engineering services in oil & gas, petrochemical and other sectors.

L&T's focus has been on heavy industrial and process plants. The company's key strengths in EPC business are its skilled manpower and inhouse state of the art fabrication facilities. The comapny has an excellent track, record of timely completion, an important parameter in the business. However, it is expected to face competition from international EPC giants like ABB Lumax, Foster Wheeler, Bechtel, Lurgi and Hyundai in future.

L&T is the market leader in the construction industry in India and offers a greater breadth of services than most of its domestic competitors. The company's cement division has grown rapidly and its capacities are presently second only to ACC. However, this division's profitability is under pressure, primarily due to the ongoing expansion programme and depressed realisations in the market during 1996/97.
The company's return on capital employed (ROCE) declined from 15.86 percent at March 1995 to 14.5 percent in March 1996 on account of an increase in the capital base finance the cement expansion.

The gearing, as measured by Total debt/Networth increased marginally from 0.32 as at March 31, 1995 to 0.40 as at March 31, 1996 inspite of a 4 billion rupees increase in term loans, because of the USD 150 million GDR placement.
Interest coverage, as measured by PBDIT/Interest & Finance charges, showed a marginal decline from 5.13 to 4.96 on account of the additional debt.
